historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Udayl Ibn Anas Al-Qarawi was the fourth rightly-guided caliph of Islam, ruling from 644 to 656 AD. The name Udayl carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Udayl is considered to be the last caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate and the first caliph of the Umayyad Caliphate.

historical_references.reference: Udayl Ibn Yasin was a prominent preacher and founder of the Al-Murabitun movement in the 11th century AD. He was born into a Berber tribe in what is now Morocco and led a campaign against the Christian Reconquistadors in Spain.
historical_references.context: Udayl is known for his military and religious accomplishments, and his movement played a significant role in the fight against the Christian Reconquistadors in the Iberian Peninsula.
